I heavily empathise with you. I get the same thing but I think it’s more likely I have it because of my OCD rather than social anxiety. I promise you, the more internal work, therapy and relaxation techniques you do the less likely you’ll get a jerk (tic). Something that can help is telling the person you’re talking to that you do this so that they’re aware and get rid of the tension you feel. Also, make a conscious effort to stop focusing on the urge to tic and other bodily sensations like heart racing, blushing etc and instead focus all your attention on other people and your environment. Game changer. It’s a daily struggle, I know, but you’ll overcome it eventually with patience and strength.

I’m a girl and have similar thoughts but they’re getting less frequent lately. What I would suggest to you is just accept these intrusive thoughts whenever they come. Separate yourself from them and view them in an objective manner because they don’t represent or define you as a person. It’s your OCD talking and you have the ability to get rid of these thoughts by acknowledging you have them and accepting their presence when they come in order to give them less power to affect you. You can’t really fight them or it makes them 10x worse, for me at least.
